newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-CAPRIATI LOOKING GOOD ON COMEBACK TRAIL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-CAPRIATI LOOKING GOOD ON COMEBACK TRAIL.

text.p: Jennifer Capriati, sentimental favourite at a tournament she won as a teenager, reached the quarter-finals of the Sydney International on Wednesday by beating Canadian Rene Simpson 6-2 6-3.
But world number Goran Ivanisevic, top seed in the men's draw at Sydney, had to overcome a scare when he lost the second set to love against Spain's Javier Sanchez.
The hard-serving Ivanisevic came back to win 6-4 0-6 6-4.
Capriati, who won the 1992 Olympic title and the Sydney tournament in 1993 at the age of 16, said it was premature to compare herself with her teenaged best.
"I don't think I've played enough (yet) to judge that or to know for myself," said the American, now on a comeback after missing most of the last three seasons with personal problems.
"I still haven't played a lot of the top players and I've really only played a few tournaments."

In the men's draw, Britain's Tim Henman, beaten finalist in the Qatar Open on Sunday, scored his second victory since arriving here from Doha by beating former double French Open champion Sergi Bruguera 3-6 6-3 6-3.
Spanish third seed Albert Costa disposed of Czech Bohdan Ulihrach Republic 6-2 6-2.
Australian Patrick Rafter outlasted Dutch eighth seed Paul Haarhuis in a three-set cliffhanger 6-7 (5-7) 7-5 7-6 (7-2).
